title: We Are South Maui: Community Plan Advisory Committee Meeting of March 8, 2023

issues.title: Village association plan to stop using injection wells
Using recycled R1 water for irrigation and firefighting
Disinfecting wastewater that reaches the ocean

recap.headline: South Maui plan committee adopts watershed, flood, wastewater and cesspool actions
recap.in_60_seconds: The South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee met with all members present to keep working on the plan's watershed management actions and its ready and resilient systems policies and actions. Three people testified: two residents and the Maui Ocean Center general manager, who also sits on the Māʻalaea Village Association board. The committee adopted more than 20 policies and actions, all without objection or by show of hands. They cover R1 recycled water reuse, buying flood-prone parcels in North Kīhei, flood rules, managed retreat, ending wastewater injection wells in Māʻalaea and South Maui, and converting cesspools in Maui Meadows and Māʻalaea. One member objected strongly to a policy on expanding R1 water reuse, saying it could open the door to more development in Wailea and Mākena, but the policy passed. Another member recused himself from the cesspool action after a Board of Ethics opinion, and a motion to ask the County Council for a three-month extension was made as the meeting recessed.

parts.title: Opening, roll call and agenda change
presented: All committee members were present.
The chair said Akaka still had no live stream for the fifth week, so the meeting was being streamed on Facebook.
The committee agreed to start with the remaining Goal 4 watershed management actions, where the last meeting left off.

parts.title: Public testimony on watershed actions and resilient systems

raised.concern: Watershed actions are good, but the plan needs ongoing monitoring of results; the testifier welcomed a new fire station and a cultural resources survey.

Funding is the main barrier for the Māʻalaea regional wastewater plant. The project is No. 6 on a State and EPA priority list of 107 projects, is estimated at about $9.5 million (about $12,500 per bedroom), and the County needs more engineers on staff.

Sediment and nutrients from cesspools and injection wells are harming the ocean; the plan should fix the watershed mauka to mākaʻi and recognize forgotten cultural sites such as a freshwater spring at Puʻuhele in Māʻalaea.
Feral pigs have damaged a mountain forest, showing the need for more fencing.

answered.said: A former council member had proposed a follow-up committee to monitor the plan after adoption, which the committee may revisit.

In response to committee questions, he said Māʻalaea has 10 injection wells and 3 have failed. Owners will pay to remove them and connect to a new force main. Maui has about 12,000 cesspools. The group will meet the mayor next week, and federal and State revolving fund money is being pursued.

next.what: Māʻalaea wastewater project briefing with the mayor

parts.title: Watershed actions: riparian zones, R1 reuse and flood-prone parcels
presented: The committee added an action to fund protection of riparian zones with fencing and native plants.
It added an action to accelerate funding for R1 water reuse on the landscape. A member said plans exist but money and capacity are the holdup.
It discussed buying flood-prone North Kīhei parcels along the Waipuʻilani and Kūlanihākoʻi gulches; a past request cited about $5.8 million.
A proposed sand dune action for Māʻalaea was found to be already covered from the February 22 meeting.

answered.said: The chair said he had written to the environmental management director to ask whether an R1 reuse plan already exists, but had not heard back.
Corporation Counsel is understaffed and cannot attend weekly; buying land under threat of condemnation can give owners tax benefits.

parts.title: Flood and coastal hazard actions 4.13 to 4.17 and new actions
presented: Adopted a repetitive-loss flood mitigation plan that must be developed and implemented.
Adopted changes to the flood hazard ordinance, including a 20-year look-back for substantial improvements, aimed at a better national flood insurance rating.
Added a flood pilot project, managed retreat, and kilo ʻāina (traditional observation) to the coastal actions, and moved the parks plan to the parks section.
Added actions for a database of coastal hazard impacts and for funded plans to let native seed banks grow and spread.

answered.said: Planning staff said a better flood rating likely brings more grants and lower flood insurance. They said one park impact is concrete and paved parking that water cannot soak through.

parts.title: Wastewater and recycled water policies
presented: Adopted a policy requiring new developments to connect to recycled water systems or be built to connect later.
Adopted gray water and recycled water use in County parks and gardens when safe; the Department of Health now allows recycled water but not gray water.
Adopted support for plan and zoning changes for a Māʻalaea wastewater plant site outside the sea level rise exposure area, and for ending injection wells in Māʻalaea and South Maui.
A member proposed a County recycled water line from the Kīhei treatment plant to Wailea for resort irrigation, to be handled as an action.

answered.said: He said the planned plant would take about 2 acres, where the highway meets Māʻalaea Road. The landowner offered the land to the County for free, and rezoning will be needed.

next.what: Recycled water line from the Kīhei plant to Wailea to be taken up as an action

parts.title: Cesspool conversion and R1 reuse policy debate
presented: A member said converting Maui Meadows cesspools could be the biggest water quality gain in South Maui, and that the governor has shown interest in State funding.
The cesspool language was moved to the actions section.
After debate, the committee adopted by show of hands a policy supporting innovative techniques for R1 water reuse.

parts.title: Resilient systems actions 3.01 to 3.05
presented: Adopted a vulnerability assessment of County infrastructure in the sea level rise exposure area.
Adopted guidance on managed relocation for owners of at-risk properties.
Adopted funding to train County staff in managed coastal retreat.
Adopted adding the sea level rise exposure area to County capital improvement planning.

answered.said: The guidance should set general rules everyone understands before helping individual owners with site plans.

parts.title: Cesspool conversion action 3.06 and a member's recusal
presented: Adopted a plan to identify and convert cesspools, with Maui Meadows by 2035 and the rest of South Maui by 2030.
The plan calls for conversion through County sewer lines or a new regional wastewater facility.
The vice chair recused himself after the Board of Ethics advised that his Maui Meadows home and association ties create a conflict.

parts.title: Extension request and recess
presented: A motion was made to ask the County Council for a three-month extension.
The meeting recessed at 9 p.m. and will resume with action 3.07.

next.what: Send extension letter to the Maui County Council

open_questions.question: Does the County already have a plan for R1 recycled water reuse in South Maui?
Does County law require new projects near R1 lines to connect to recycled water, as it does for sewer?
How much would it cost to buy the flood-prone parcels along the Waipuʻilani and Kūlanihākoʻi gulches?
When will Akaka live stream these committee meetings again?

not_on_tracker.topic: Cesspool conversion in Maui Meadows and Māʻalaea
not_on_tracker.why: Cesspool owners face required conversion and costs, and runoff affects South Maui's ocean water.

not_on_tracker.topic: Buying flood-prone parcels in North Kīhei gulches
not_on_tracker.why: Neighbors want the gulches kept open to prevent flooding and to allow a long-planned greenway.
Pig damage harms the watershed that feeds South Maui's water and reefs.

not_on_tracker.topic: Managed retreat from the South Maui coast
not_on_tracker.why: Shoreline owners and the County will need rules, staff and money to move out of harm's way.

not_on_tracker.topic: Board of Ethics recusal of committee members
not_on_tracker.why: Residents who serve on the committee may be barred from voting on their own neighborhoods.

moments.quote: They also said that if Maui County takes this over, we will give this land to Maui County for free.
moments.about: Explains that the landowner has offered the proposed Māʻalaea wastewater plant site to the County, the land behind a plan policy supporting rezoning for that facility.

moments.who: a South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee member
moments.quote: This basically just takes the treated water to the largest water user in the county so that they aren't using potable water for irrigation.
moments.about: Explains a proposed recycled water line from the Kīhei treatment plant to Wailea resorts so that irrigation would use reclaimed water instead of drinking water.

moments.who: a Kīhei homeowner serving on the advisory committee
moments.quote: But there was a problem. The county wasn't able to help us to find where the lateral tie-in was.
moments.about: A first-hand account of the cost and difficulty of converting a cesspool to county sewer, which shaped support for grant-backed cesspool conversion actions in the plan.
